notes: Scope: scan 098 alone was read. The original page was viewed once for layout and each native half once. All 14 saved first-pass crops were subsequently inspected. An initial graph_original display was truncated before a usable image was delivered; the same saved crop was then displayed successfully. Existing crops were reused for later letter and line-count checks; the original and halves were not revisited. No OCR, recognition software, external research or TeX compilation was used.

Source claim: for the strict case written S-prime simeq S and I-prime isomorphism-arrow I coproduct tilded J, G-prime is obtained by choosing ordinary edges C, placing a point on each selected edge and cutting there. The text relates this to cutting X along the finite marked part. These are statements of the manuscript; their general validity was not proved in this pass.

Source claim in the lower margin: the inverse construction specifies a fixed-point-free involution on the branches called aplaties and glues their ends. The subsequent unfinished paragraph additionally removes selected such branches and retains a union of connected components. No continuation beyond the final c'est was supplied.

The only mathematical check actually performed was the local incidence check of the two drawn examples, recorded below. General normalization statements and the general involution construction were not independently proved.

The upper graph has five marked positions, five complete edge strokes including the right loop, three original free branches and two crosses placed on edge interiors. The lower picture retains those marked positions, replaces the two crossed connections by four further free ends and has two components. The open centre of the lower-left endpoint mark is a graphic fact only; no new vertex semantics is inferred.
The lower drawing is explicitly labelled G without a prime, despite the prose introducing the result as G-prime. This is a possible source slip; the written G is preserved.

The outer opening parenthesis before the complement description and the inner opening before the hatted-I map have only one closing parenthesis after that map. C's added second closer is removed. The later i.e parenthesis is separate and its closing stroke after X is retained.

At the foot, baseline en survives before the cancelled word, while a distinct raised en begins the replacement en outre. The strike extends through the old right parenthesis. The duplicate en and unmatched surviving opening are preserved without grammatical or punctuation repair.

The compact overlined m and the separate equality-shaped sign are transcribed literally. Their expansion as même is inferred from their prose positions and is confined to the abbreviations list; neither is silently replaced by the word. The second sign has two bars and cannot be the et printed by C.

The opening ens. has a detached full stop; marginal ens does not. The cutting abbreviation has a stop after i but none after e. The curve after ordinaires belongs to its insertion leader, not to a detached comma.

All four complete adjective occurrences were inspected separately and read aplaties. The cancelled noun flèches|pieds was not resolved merely because flèches is strongly favoured; the strike prevents letter-by-letter certification.

All five C deletion groups and all four C insertion groups were checked separately. No insertion on this page was found to be itself cancelled. The enlarged scope of the last deletion includes a legible closing parenthesis.

Top folio 48 is dark and graphically consistent with the body hand. Lower folio 97 is paler and pencil-like; its authorship is not established by this scan. H acknowledges 48 editorially but omits 97.

H's editorial drawing synopsis and re-reading note are not source text and are not added to the TeX. Its note about the right free segment in the first drawing agrees with the ink. The actual drawing differences are recorded against its supplied drawing descriptions.

The lower inverse-margin crop clips the far-right part of its first G at the crop edge; the glyph was complete in the initially viewed native half. The future blind box is widened rightward to include it. Some saved crop edges contain neighbouring line fragments, which were used only as context.

Confidence and error flags are separated: resolving a C choice to its first option does not by itself count as a C error. The uncertain old préservant candidate does not establish a settled lexical error in H's illegible placeholder; H's omissions of wholly visible cancelled groups and its definite punctuation-state errors are still recorded.

check_events.outcome: After visually reading both complete drawing crops, counted the five marked positions and their incidences twice. The upper picture has three original free branches; cutting the crossed central connection and crossed right loop creates four further free ends, for seven in the lower picture. The central cut separates the left and right marked-position groups; the loop cut does not further separate them. Thus the lower picture's two components and branch placements agree with the two indicated local cuts. Pairing the two horizontal stubs and the two lower right stubs restores the corresponding upper connections. This check concerns only the drawn example and does not prove the general normalization or involution claims.
